purpose: Define how Recovery collects valid evidence for curriculum outcomes through topic verification, cumulative checkpoints and school-like mocks without collapsing all competence into a single grammar score.
principles: Assessment scope is derived from the learner's official school recovery programme and its required Curriculum v2 outcomes, not from the full Sblocco catalogue.
Topic verification is useful local evidence but cannot by itself prove year-level transfer or Recovery readiness.
Cumulative assessments must conceal which grammar or language system is being tested whenever transfer is the evidence target.
Every assessment stores evidence by primary competence axis and outcome; an overall mark must never erase a blocking weakness in a required axis.
Listening and functional/oral communication are included only when the learner's programme or selected school-assessment profile requires them.
Assessment difficulty comes from independent selection, integration and school-like task demands, not obscure vocabulary or trick questions.
Exact questions used for teaching or topic verification must not be copied into mocks as transfer evidence.
The blueprint defines evidence shape and composition. Numeric readiness thresholds and compensation rules belong to readiness-policy.json.

evidence_sources.role: Confirm independent control of one topic after Recupera, Allenati and Modalità scuola.
evidence_sources.reuse_policy: May contribute supporting evidence, but year-exit transfer requires cumulative or mock evidence as well.

evidence_sources.role: Sample several currently required outcomes in mixed form so the plan can detect transfer weaknesses before the final phase.
evidence_sources.reuse_policy: Questions must be unseen or substantially transformed from topic verification items.

evidence_sources.role: Provide an exam-like cumulative performance sample across the learner's active programme while there is still time to change priorities.
evidence_sources.reuse_policy: Use a distinct form from checkpoint and final mock; do not reveal target rules in task titles.

evidence_sources.role: Collect the strongest pre-exam transfer evidence on the outcomes and assessment formats required by the learner's school programme.
evidence_sources.reuse_policy: Must use a fresh assessment form and must not copy exact teaching, topic-verify or intermediate-mock questions.

programme_scope_policy.source_of_truth: required Curriculum v2 outcomes derived from the learner's official school recovery programme
programme_scope_policy.default_year_profile_role: fills the initial outcome set only when the school programme does not specify enough detail
programme_scope_policy.active_axis_definition: a competence axis is active when at least one required outcome on that axis belongs to the learner's programme
programme_scope_policy.optional_axis_rule: listening and functional_communication do not become active merely because the year profile contains them; their programme_requirement and the learner's declared assessment profile must be respected
programme_scope_policy.topic_relationship: grammar topic mappings can select suitable fragments, but topic completion never substitutes for required skill/outcome coverage
programme_scope_policy.unknown_programme_rule: when the school programme is incomplete, prefer the robust year profile and explicitly mark inferred requirements so they can be changed later

sampling_priority: required blocking-candidate outcomes with insufficient cumulative transfer evidence
required outcomes with weak diagnostic, topic-verify or prior checkpoint evidence
repeated error patterns that affect more than one required outcome
breadth across remaining required active axes
representative high-frequency school task formats from the learner's programme

all_assessments: Every scored fragment declares one primary competence axis and one or more outcome_ids.
Secondary axes may receive supporting evidence only when the task genuinely samples them.
If only one axis is active, the assessment may be single-axis; otherwise cumulative assessment must not silently omit active blocking-candidate axes merely to preserve a fixed grammar quota.
Grammar and lexical items embedded inside reading, writing or listening may provide secondary evidence, but they do not automatically count as independent grammar or lexical transfer evidence.

checkpoint.target_active_axis_coverage: min(all active axes, 3) with priority to under-evidenced blocking candidates
checkpoint.exceptions: The ceiling does not apply when the official programme is grammar-only or when only grammar_sentence_control is active.

mock_intermediate.target_active_axis_coverage: all active blocking-candidate axes that fit the session budget, then breadth across remaining required axes
mock_intermediate.exceptions: The ceiling does not apply when fewer than three axes are active or the official school test is explicitly grammar-dominant.

mock_final.target_active_axis_coverage: all active blocking-candidate axes, plus representative evidence for every other active core axis when the time budget permits
mock_final.exceptions: The ceiling may be exceeded only when the official school assessment format or required outcome set justifies it.

checkpoint.purpose: Detect whether isolated topic gains transfer into mixed school-style performance and update remediation priorities.
checkpoint.target_fragment_count: 4-7 depending on fragment duration and active axes
required_properties: no rule labels that reveal the target
at least one unseen or mixed-context fragment
at least one controlled-production or transfer-production fragment when grammar or writing is active

mock_intermediate.purpose: Simulate the learner's likely recovery-test demands early enough for the plan to respond to weaknesses.
mock_intermediate.target_fragment_count: 5-9 depending on required writing/listening tasks and school format
required_properties: no coaching or explanations during the attempt
task order mixes language systems where school-appropriate
required reading, writing, listening or communication axes receive dedicated primary evidence rather than being inferred from grammar items
results feed priority changes but do not alone declare READY

mock_final.purpose: Collect the strongest final transfer sample before the school recovery assessment across the outcomes the learner is actually required to demonstrate.
mock_final.target_fragment_count: 6-10 depending on required extended tasks and session mode
required_properties: fresh unseen form distinct from previous cumulative assessments
no teaching, hints, rule labels or immediate corrections
all active blocking-candidate axes sampled when feasible within the declared school-test profile
at least two distinct transfer assessment modes when two or more are valid for the programme
integrated production included when writing or functional communication is required
per-axis and per-outcome evidence retained for readiness evaluation
global score may be displayed as a summary but cannot override blocking outcome evidence

assessment_fragment_contract.purpose: Define the reusable unit from which checkpoint and mock sessions can be materialized dynamically for the learner's required outcome set.

field_contract.fragment_id: Stable source identity independent of a generated assignment or learner.
field_contract.year_profiles: Default compatible school-year profiles; the school programme may override them.
field_contract.primary_axis: Single competence axis receiving primary scored evidence.
field_contract.secondary_axes: Optional supporting evidence axes; [] is valid.
field_contract.outcome_ids: One or more Curriculum v2 outcomes genuinely sampled by the fragment.
field_contract.assessment_modes: One or more modes from assessment-modes.json.
field_contract.estimated_minutes: Expected learner time used by dynamic materialization budgets.
field_contract.difficulty_band: CEFR/task-demand band appropriate to the outcome evidence.
field_contract.school_task_family: Human-readable family such as mixed grammar, reading text, translation, guided/independent writing or listening.
field_contract.transfer_level: controlled_performance or transfer; cumulative mocks should prioritize transfer.
field_contract.content_source_policy: Must indicate whether the fragment is unseen, transformed or reusable; exact teaching-item copies are not valid mock transfer evidence.

selection_rules: Prefer approved fragments whose outcome_ids intersect the learner's required under-evidenced outcomes.
Do not select two near-duplicate fragments merely to increase question count.
Do not exceed the session time budget after the first selected fragment unless no valid smaller fragment exists.
Preserve enough time for required writing, listening or oral fragments before filling remaining time with short grammar items.
Where multiple equivalent fragments exist, rotate forms to reduce exact item reuse across checkpoint and mocks.

anti_false_readiness_rules: A learner who has only topic_verify evidence for an outcome has not yet demonstrated cumulative year-level transfer.
A strong global mock mark cannot erase a weak required blocking-candidate outcome or axis; the future readiness policy must inspect disaggregated evidence.
Grammar accuracy inside a reading or writing task cannot by itself establish reading or writing competence, and the reverse is also true.
Recognition-heavy success must not replace required production evidence.
Repeated exposure to the same item or near-identical item cannot be counted as independent transfer evidence.
An axis that is not part of the student's programme must not lower readiness merely because no evidence was collected for it.
